ai.description: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* is a small shrub frog (SVL ~18–20 mm) with a yellowish-brown dorsum and distinct reddish-brown blotches. It features a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow patch on the posterior side of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small invertebrates within its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Munnar region in Kerala’s Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes primarrumpfi* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
